newsitem.title: USA: AmEx launches Central American card.
newsitem.headline: AmEx launches Central American card.

text.p: American Express Co. and privately held card-issuer Credomatic said on Thursday they launched the American Express card in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Guatemala and Honduras.
The card, which allows holders to pay bills in local currencies or U.S. dollars, will be launched later this year in El Salvador, they added.

Credomatic, based in San Jose, Costa Rica, describes itself as the leading card issuer in Central America with a network of more than 36,000 merchants and more than 700,000 cards in its portfolio. It also issues Visa and MasterCards.
Credomatic will be responsible for all operations supporting the American Express card and will market the card in the five Central American markets.
American Express said customers in the markets will have access to the American Express international service network and other travel and financial services.

American Express previously provided a U.S. dollar-denominated American Express Card to Central American customers. Existing card members in the five countries will have the option of converting their cards to the new product, retaining their dollar-denominated card, or carrying both.
None of the financial arrangements between American Express and Credomatic were disclosed.
James Cracchiolo, president of American Express global network servies group, said in a telephone conference call the company will make two additional announcements of partnershps in coming weeks.
